import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 85

*Carbery’s rectangle problem*

References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.85)
- [CCW99] Carbery, Anthony, Michael Christ, and James Wright. "Multidimensional van der Corput and sublevel set estimates." Journal of the American Mathematical Society 12.4 (1999): 981-1015 Section 6.
- [Ke00] Keleti, Tamás. "Density and covering properties of intervals of ℝn." Mathematika 47.1-2 (2000): 229-242.
- [KKM02] Katz, Nets Hawk, Elliot Krop, and Mauro Maggioni. "Remarks on the box problem." Mathematical Research Letters 9.4 (2002): 515-520.
- [Mu02] Mubayi, Dhruv. "Some exact results and new asymptotics for hypergraph Turán numbers." Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 11.3 (2002): 299-309 Conjecture 1.4.
- [CPZ20] Conlon, David, Cosmin Pohoata, and Dmitriy Zakharov. "Random multilinear maps and the Erd\H {o} s box problem." arXiv preprint arXiv:2011.09024 (2020).
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory Set Topology

namespace Green85

/--
Suppose that $A$ is an open subset of $[0, 1]^2$ with measure $\alpha$. Are there four points in
$A$ determining an axis-parallel rectangle with area $\gt c \alpha^2$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 28 52]
theorem green_85 :
  answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ A : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
    IsOpen A →
    A ⊆ Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1 →
    A.Nonempty →
    let α := (volume A).toReal
    ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂,
      {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧
      c * α ^ 2 ≤ |x₁ - x₂| * |y₁ - y₂| := by
  sorry

/--
From [Gr24] "It is quite easy to show using Cauchy-Schwarz that there must be such a rectangle with
area $\gg \alpha^2 (\log 1/\alpha)^{-1}$."
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 28 52]
theorem green_85_loose :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝[>] 0,
    ∀ A : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
    IsOpen A →
    A ⊆ Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1 →
    A.Nonempty →
    α = (volume A).toReal →
    ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂,
      {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧
      c * α ^ 2 * (Real.log (1/α))⁻¹ ≤ |x₁ - x₂| * |y₁ - y₂| := by
  sorry

end Green85

findings.description: The module docstring's [KKM02] reference (line 28) gives the page range 515–520. The cited paper occupies pages 515–519. Neither theorem's mathematics is affected.
findings.source_evidence: The published PDF of Katz, Krop and Maggioni, “Remarks on the box problem,” begins “Mathematical Research Letters 9, 515–519 (2002)” and ends on page 519: https://intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/mrl/2002/0009/0004/MRL-2002-0009-0004-a011.pdf. Green's bibliography, reference [188], also gives 515–519.
findings.suggested_fix: Change “515-520” to “515-519” in the [KKM02] bibliographic entry.

reformulations.difference: Positive measure and four distinct rectangle vertices are encoded by A.Nonempty and the positive lower area bound, rather than by explicit measure-positivity and coordinate-distinctness hypotheses.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an open subset A of the unit square, volume A ≤ 1, so .toReal has no infinite-measure default case, and A.Nonempty is equivalent to 0 < (volume A).toReal. Thus c > 0 implies c * α² > 0. The area inequality forces both x₁ ≠ x₂ and y₁ ≠ y₂, making the four displayed coordinate pairs distinct. Their absolute-difference product is precisely the rectangle's area. The quantified equivalence with explicit positive measure and distinct coordinates was proved as Review.positive_distinct_form_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The Lean gives a uniform estimate for sufficiently small positive α. CCW Proposition 6.1, underlying Green's logarithmic estimate, uses an all-density bound with log⁺(t) = max(1, log t).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For open subsets of the unit square these formulations are equivalent up to an absolute constant. The all-density bound immediately gives the eventual statement when α < exp(-1). Conversely, suppose the eventual bound holds below ε with constant c. Fix 0 < t < 1 with t² < min(ε, exp(-1)) and apply it to tA, whose measure is t²α. Scaling the resulting rectangle back gives area at least c t² α² / (log(1/α) + K), where K = log(1/t²) > 0. Since 0 < α ≤ 1, log(1/α) + K ≤ (1 + K) max(1, log(1/α)), giving the all-density estimate with constant c t²/(1 + K). The filter-to-positive-threshold equivalence was checked in Lean; this full scaling equivalence was not formalized.

review.notes: No substantive misformalization was found in either theorem. Green's current list still presents Problem 85 as open, and CCW Proposition 6.1 establishes the logarithmically weaker bound, consistent with both category tags. Scratch checks compile with zero errors and warnings and establish finite positive measure, the bound α ≤ 1, nondegenerate vertices, a nontrivial right-neighborhood filter, and realization of every density 0 < α ≤ 1 by an open strip. The main docstring's strict inequality is harmless: halving the existential constant proves equivalence with the non-strict inequality, also checked in Lean. The test/equivalence lemmas do not depend on sorryAx. Keleti's full text was inaccessible; its publisher abstract and Green's discussion were read, and neither declaration formalizes its separate intersection-area variant. The reviewed file remains byte-identical to the specified commit; no repository files were edited.
